meta.title: Scoutr — say it, ship it
meta.description: Scoutr turns a typed, spoken or meeting prompt into a finished, tested product: apps, sites, APIs, media, decks and agents. Quality-gated, secure by default, fairly priced, EU-hosted.

cookie.title: Cookies, briefly

hero.lede: Type it, say it, or invite Scoutr to your meeting. It plans, designs, builds and tests real apps, sites, APIs, media, decks and agents — and shows you the price before it starts.
hero.prompt1: A booking site for my ceramics studio, with Swish payments and a waitlist
hero.prompt2: Turn yesterday's customer meeting into a spec, then build the MVP
hero.prompt3: An agent that drafts replies to support email every morning — ask me before sending
hero.badge: Hosted in the EU · Pay only when it works

why.lede: Other builders give you a demo. Scoutr gives you something you can put your name on.

quality.title: Proven quality
quality.body: Every build passes typecheck, lint, unit, integration and end-to-end tests before you see “done”. Failing gates come with a proposed fix.

design.title: Award-level design
design.body: Each project gets three art directions, real design tokens and motion that respects reduced-motion. A vision review scores every viewport.

security.title: Security by default
security.body: Semgrep, secret scanning, dependency audits, row-level security and auth checks run on every change. Insecure apps don't deploy.
security.proof: Deploys are blocked until gates pass

pricing.title: Fair pricing
pricing.body: You see an estimate before work starts and set hard spend caps. If the agent fails, you aren't charged — and we show you that too.

lockin.title: No lock-in
lockin.body: It's your code: standard stacks, exportable to GitHub in one click, deployable anywhere. Decks export to PPTX and PDF.
lockin.proof: Export to GitHub · PPTX · PDF · DOCX

eu.title: EU data
eu.body: Projects, recordings and transcripts are stored in Frankfurt. GDPR export and deletion are a button, not a support ticket.

how.title: Four steps from idea to live.

ask.title: Ask
ask.body: Type, use your voice, or invite the Scoutr notetaker to a meeting and approve the spec it writes.

estimate.title: See the price
estimate.body: Scoutr classifies the request, asks one question if it must, and shows a cost range before it spends a cent.

build.title: Watch it build
build.body: Plan, design and code stream into a live preview. Edit visually, comment, or co-edit the code in real time.

ship.title: Ship and own it
ship.body: Gates pass, it deploys with your domain and TLS. Roll back any checkpoint or take the code with you.

how.lede: You stay in control at every step — and can see exactly what the agent is doing.

pricing.body: Estimates come before work, spend caps are hard limits, and tasks that fail because of the agent are never charged.
pricing.examplePrompt: A landing page with a waitlist and Stripe checkout
pricing.point1: An estimate and a hard spend cap before any work starts
pricing.point2: Estimate vs. charged shown on every task
pricing.point3: Failed because of the agent? You pay nothing

eu.title: Built in Europe. Stored in Europe.
eu.body: Your projects, meeting recordings, transcripts and secrets stay in the EU. Encryption at rest, a data processing agreement for every customer, and retention you control.

final.body: Free to start. You only pay for work that succeeds.

statement.label: What Scoutr is
statement.lead: Scoutr is the shortest path from an idea to a product you can ship.
statement.rest: Describe what you need. Scoutr picks a proven stack, writes the code, proves that it works and hands you everything it made — code, tests, designs and a running preview.

ctaCard.title: Ready when you are.
ctaCard.body: Describe your idea. You'll see the plan and the price before anything is built.

make.title: One prompt. Every kind of output.
make.lede: The same workspace builds software, media, documents and agents — and holds all of it to the same quality bar.

apps.title: Apps, sites and APIs
apps.body: Next.js web apps, Expo mobile apps, marketing sites and FastAPI backends — with sign-in, a database, row-level security and tests from the very first commit.

media.title: Images and video
media.body: On-brand images and Remotion videos from a sentence, rendered, stored in your project and editable with the next prompt.

docs.title: Decks and documents
docs.body: Slide decks and documents written from your notes or a meeting, edited in the browser and exported to PPTX, PDF and DOCX.

agents.title: Agents and meetings
agents.body: Invite Scoutr to a meeting and it turns the conversation into a spec. Or build an agent that runs on a schedule, asks before it acts and logs every step.

crew.title: Eight specialists. One conversation.
crew.lede: Scoutr splits your ask into steps and hands each one to the specialist that knows it best — then brings it back to you as one tested result.
crew.hint: Every message in the project timeline comes from one of them, so you always know who did what.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Scoutr, a service that generates software, media, documents and automated agents from your instructions. Please read them carefully.
terms.s1: Scoutr is operated by Scoutr AB, a company registered in Sweden (“Scoutr”, “we”). Contact: legal@forge.example. These terms form an agreement between you (or the organisation you represent) and Scoutr.
terms.s2: You must provide accurate information and keep your credentials secure. You are responsible for activity in your workspace. Workspace owners decide who has access and with which role.
terms.s3: You keep all rights to the prompts, files, recordings and other material you provide, and to the code, media and documents Scoutr generates for you, subject to third-party licences of included open-source components. You grant Scoutr a limited licence to process your content only to provide the service.
terms.s4: You may not use Scoutr to create malware, phishing or impersonation sites, to harvest credentials, to infringe others’ rights, or to process personal data unlawfully. We scan deployments for abuse and may take down content that violates these rules.
terms.s5: When you record a meeting or invite the Scoutr notetaker, you are responsible for informing participants and obtaining any consent required by law. The notetaker announces itself in the meeting chat.
terms.s6: Paid usage is billed according to your plan. We show an estimate before a task starts; spend caps you set are enforced as hard limits. Tasks that fail due to an error on our side are not charged.
terms.s7: We aim for high availability but the service is provided “as is”. We may change features with reasonable notice. Material changes to these terms will be announced at least 30 days in advance.
terms.s8: To the extent permitted by law, Scoutr’s total liability is limited to the fees you paid in the 12 months before the claim. Nothing limits liability that cannot be limited under applicable law, including for gross negligence.
terms.s9: You can delete your account at any time from Settings. We may suspend accounts that seriously breach these terms. On termination you can export your data for 30 days.
terms.s10: These terms are governed by Swedish law. Disputes are settled by the courts of Sweden, without prejudice to mandatory consumer protection rules in your country of residence.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data Scoutr processes, why, and the rights you have under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
privacy.s1: Scoutr AB, Sweden, is the controller for account data. For content you upload into a workspace (for example meeting recordings), your organisation is the controller and Scoutr acts as processor under our Data Processing Agreement.
privacy.s2: Account data (name, email, password hash, language), workspace and project content, prompts and voice input, meeting audio and transcripts you choose to record, usage and billing records, and security logs (IP address, audit trail).
privacy.s3: Providing the service (contract, Art. 6(1)(b)); security, abuse prevention and audit logs (legitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f)); billing and bookkeeping (legal obligation, Art. 6(1)(c)); remembering preferences (consent, Art. 6(1)(a)).
privacy.s4: Data is stored in the EU (Frankfurt, eu-central-1). Where a sub-processor outside the EEA is involved, we rely on adequacy decisions or Standard Contractual Clauses and minimise what is shared.
privacy.s5: Meeting recordings are kept for 30 days and transcripts for 365 days by default; workspace admins can shorten these periods. Event history is kept for 180 days. Deleted accounts are anonymised immediately.
privacy.s6: You can access and export your data (Settings → Export my data), correct it, delete your account (Settings → Delete account), object to processing, and lodge a complaint with the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY).
privacy.s7: Essential cookies: forge_session (keeps you signed in), forge_consent (your cookie choice). Preference cookies, only stored across visits with your consent: forge_locale (language) and forge_theme (theme). We do not use advertising or third-party tracking cookies.
privacy.s8: Our data protection contact is privacy@forge.example.

dpa.title: Data Processing Agreement
dpa.intro: This Data Processing Agreement (DPA) forms part of the Terms of Service when Scoutr processes personal data on behalf of a customer, in line with Article 28 GDPR.
dpa.s1: The customer is the controller and Scoutr is the processor for personal data contained in customer content, including meeting recordings, transcripts, project data and agent inputs.
dpa.s2: Scoutr processes personal data only on the customer’s documented instructions, which are given through the use of the service and these terms, unless required otherwise by EU or member state law.
dpa.s3: Personnel with access are bound by confidentiality. Scoutr applies encryption in transit and at rest, envelope-encrypted secrets, role-based access, audit logging, isolated build sandboxes and regular security testing.
dpa.s4: Scoutr maintains a list of sub-processors (hosting, model providers, transcription, email) and gives at least 30 days’ notice of changes, during which the customer may object.
dpa.s5: Scoutr assists the customer with data subject requests, data protection impact assessments and breach notifications. Personal data breaches are reported without undue delay and within 48 hours.
dpa.s6: On termination, or on request, Scoutr deletes or returns customer personal data. Meeting data can be deleted by the customer at any time from the meeting page.
dpa.s7: Scoutr makes available the information necessary to demonstrate compliance and allows for audits, including inspections, by the customer or an auditor mandated by the customer, with reasonable notice.

meetings.consentBody: You must tell participants the meeting is being recorded and transcribed, and get consent where the law requires it. The notetaker announces itself; anyone can ask you to remove it. Recordings are stored in the EU and deleted automatically after the retention period.
meetings.recordLede: Record an in-person meeting from this browser. Audio uploads in resumable chunks, so a dropped connection doesn't lose anything.

scoutr.desc: Takes your ask, splits it into steps, hands each one to the right specialist and reports back to you.

plania.desc: Turns your words into a spec and a task list you can approve before anything is built.

pixel.desc: Proposes art directions, design tokens and motion — and scores every viewport.

byggo.desc: Writes the code, installs packages, runs the app and keeps the live preview fresh.

vakt.desc: Runs the quality gates — tests, lint, security scans — and blocks anything unsafe.

revy.desc: Reads the result like a senior engineer and sends back anything that isn't good enough.

chatti.desc: Answers questions about your project in plain language. Nothing is built or charged.

mailo.desc: Runs your scheduled agents and email workflows, and asks before anything is sent.
